```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6)
```

This document generates every figure and table of the master's thesis
*Fine-scale distribution of plant eDNA in a tropical rainforest* (Université
des Antilles, 2026) that comes from the data. It follows the order of the report.

The study compares two views of the plants of the Petit Plateau plot (Nouragues
reserve, French Guiana): a botanical inventory of the stems, and the plant DNA
found in soil samples taken every 10 m, with three genetic markers.

# How to use this document

Open `ADNe_Nourague_2026.Rproj` in RStudio and knit this file, or run the chunks
in order. The working directory must be the folder of this file.

The long computations (`df_H1`, `df_H3`, `df_RF`...) are saved in
`ADNe_Nourague_2026_files/` the first time and read from there afterwards. Set
`RECOMPUTE` to `TRUE` below to run them again from the raw data. The random
forests then give slightly different values from the report.

```{r load}
RECOMPUTE <- FALSE

source("data_import.R") # Paths and reading of the raw data
source("grid.R")        # Spatial grids of the plot
source("table.R")       # Tables behind the figures
source("plots.R")       # Figures

set.seed(123)
```

## Files

| Module           | Content                                                      |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `data_import.R`  | Paths of the project and functions reading the raw data      |
| `grid.R`         | Spatial grids, with the description of all their parameters  |
| `table.R`        | Taxa lists, relative richness, growth forms, correlations    |
| `plots.R`        | One function for each figure                                 |

## Data

All the data are in the folder `Data-Nouragues-2026/`, next to the folder of this program.

| Data                  | File                                                       | Source                    |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Botanical inventories | `Bota/Nour_2012.csv`, `Nour_2022.csv`                      | G. Sellan, A. Mirabelle   |
| eDNA (MOTUs × samples) | `Irene_genet/*.rds`                                       | I. Calderón, A. Maniouloux |
| Samples and environment | `Zinger_plants_nouragues/Zinger_et_al_metabar_PP1_samples.txt` | L. Zinger             |
| Reference checklist   | `Zinger_plants_nouragues/Plants_Nouragues2001.xls`         | Bongers et al. (2001)     |
| Morphological traits  | `Giacomo_plant_morpho/Appendix_S2-6___S8-13.xlsx`          | Vleminckx et al. (2021)   |

## Vocabulary

| Term               | Meaning                                                                 |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Bota               | Botanical inventory of 2012 (2022 is only used in Figure 5)             |
| REF                | Reference checklist of the plants of the Nouragues high-forest          |
| Sper01, ITS2, 18S  | Genetic markers of the eDNA surveys                                     |
| Presence (I.O)     | Presence of the taxon, compared with the Matthews correlation coefficient |
| Count              | Number of stems of the taxon within a radius                            |
| HYP, EXP           | Models of the eDNA signal from the stems, hyperbolic and exponential decay with distance (see `grid.R`) |
| H1                 | Hill number of order 1, the exponential of the Shannon index            |
| `df_H1` to `df_H4` | Results of the four analyses: richness by family, abundance, spatial correlations, diversity |

# Taxonomic detection

## Table 1 {#table-1}

Percentage of species richness by growth form in the reference checklist.

```{r table-1}
knitr::kable(tab_all_growth(), col.names = c("Growth form", "Proportion (%)"))
```

## Taxa lists

List of the taxa detected by each survey at each taxonomic level, used by
Figures 2, 7 and S1.

```{r taxa-lists}
list_by_level <- cached("list_by_level", recompute = RECOMPUTE, function(){

  config_tab <- expand.grid(
    "Marker" = c("Bota","Sper01","ITS2","18S","REF"),
    "Level" = c("Family","Genus","Species"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  config_tab$tax_list <- map2(config_tab$Level, config_tab$Marker, get_tax_list)

  # list_by_level[[Level]][[Survey]]
  config_tab %>%
    split(.$Level) %>%
    map(~ setNames(.x$tax_list, .x$Marker))
})

# Merge the three eDNA markers into one survey
list_by_level_edna <- map(list_by_level, function(x){
  list(
    Bota = x[["Bota"]],
    eDNA = unique(c(x[["Sper01"]], x[["ITS2"]], x[["18S"]])),
    REF  = x[["REF"]]
  )
})
```

## Figure 2 {#figure-2}

Taxa shared between the reference checklist, the botanical survey and the
combined eDNA surveys, at the family, genus and species levels.

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 4}
plot_venn_levels(list_by_level_edna)
```

## Figure 3 {#figure-3}

**Input.** `df_H1` gives the share of the MOTUs (eDNA) or of the species (Bota)
of each family, in percentage. Only the rarefied eDNA data are used, and the
botanical species are counted in squares of 10 × 10 m around each position.

**Figure.** (a) Relative richness of the families in each survey. Families in
orange, green and red are only present in the reference, in the botanical survey
and in the eDNA surveys, those in blue are in both surveys. (b) Estimated share
of the growth forms: each family is split according to the growth forms of its
species in the reference checklist.

```{r df-H1}
df_H1 <- cached("df_H1", recompute = RECOMPUTE, function(){

  config_genet <- expand.grid(
    Type = "genet",
    Rar = TRUE,
    Marker = c("Sper01","ITS2","18S"),
    Level = "Family",
    Metric = "OTU",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  config_bota <- expand.grid(
    Type = "bota",
    Year = "2012",
    Level = "Family",
    Metric = "OTU",
    Radius = "pixel",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  test_ab_rel_sum(bind_rows(config_genet, config_bota))
})
```

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7}
df_list <- family_richness_list(df_H1)

# Families with their order and colors
df_ab_rel <- bind_rows(df_list) %>%
  left_join(fam_order_col(df_list), by = "Clade")

p_families <- ab_rel_plot(df_ab_rel, treshold_label = 10)
p_growth <- growth_form_plot(growth_form_source(df_ab_rel))

p_families | p_growth
```

## Figure 4 {#figure-4}

Relation between the reads and the basal area of the families, on the families
shared by the botanical survey and each marker. On this log-log scale, a slope
of 1 means that the structure of the community is unchanged, a slope above 1
that the dominant families are amplified in eDNA, and a slope below 1 that they
are attenuated.

```{r figure-4}
df_H2 <- cached("df_H2", recompute = RECOMPUTE, function(){

  # Basal area and percentage of tree species of each family
  bota_families <- import_bota(list("Year" = 2012)) %>%
    rank_ab_tib_bota_BA("Family") %>%
    inner_join(
      tab_family_growth() %>% dplyr::select(Family = family, tree),
      by = "Family"
    )

  # Reads of each family, for a marker
  marker_families <- function(marker){
    import_genet(list("Marker" = marker, "Rar" = TRUE)) %>%
      rank_ab_tib_genet("family") %>%
      dplyr::rename(Family = family) %>%
      dplyr::select(Family, Reads) %>%
      mutate(Marker = marker)
  }

  map_dfr(c("Sper01","ITS2"), ~ inner_join(bota_families, marker_families(.x), by = "Family"))
})

plot_log_log(df_H2)
```

# Spatial patterns

## Correlations between surveys

**Input.** `df_H3` compares the spatial pattern of each taxon shared by the
botanical survey and a marker, at each taxonomic level.

The botanical pattern comes from four methods (see `grid.R`):

- **Presence (I.O)**: at least one stem within 10 m. It is compared with the
  presence in eDNA by the Matthews correlation coefficient.
- **Count**: number of stems within 10 m.
- **HYP**: stems weighted by their size, with a hyperbolic decay with distance
  (α = 1.79).
- **EXP**: stems weighted by their size, with an exponential decay with distance
  (α = 1.79, β = 0.1).

The last three are compared with the number of reads by a Spearman correlation.

```{r df-H3}
df_H3 <- cached("df_H3", recompute = RECOMPUTE, function(){

  basic_config <- expand.grid(
    "g.Rar" = TRUE,
    "g.Marker" = c("Sper01","ITS2","18S"),
    "b.Year" = 2012,
    "Level" = c("Species", "Genus", "Family"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  config_tab <- bind_rows(
    crossing(basic_config, "Metric_corr" = "I.O",   "b.Radius" = 10,    "Norm" = FALSE),
    crossing(basic_config, "Metric_corr" = "Count", "b.Radius" = 10,    "Norm" = TRUE),
    crossing(basic_config, "Metric_corr" = "EXP",   "b.Radius" = 10000, "Alpha" = 1.79, "Beta" = 0.1, "Norm" = TRUE),
    crossing(basic_config, "Metric_corr" = "HYP",   "b.Radius" = 10000, "Alpha" = 1.79, "Norm" = TRUE)
  )

  # One row per taxon shared by the botanical survey and the marker
  level_list <- filter_common_taxa(list_by_level)

  config_tab <- config_tab %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(Name = list(level_list[[Level]][[g.Marker]])) %>%
    unnest(Name)

  make_cor_table(config_tab)
})
```

## Figure 5 {#figure-5}

eDNA distribution of four species with the Sper01 marker. Red and orange circles
are the stems of the 2012 and 2022 inventories. `selection` gives the ranks of
the species among the 19 species of `df_H3`, sorted by increasing correlation.

```{r figure-5, fig.height = 5}
patch_turbo_ex(df_H3,
               marker = "Sper01",
               level = "Species",
               metric = "EXP",
               selection = c(19,9,13,2),
               n = 4)
```

## Figure 6 {#figure-6}

Botanical models for *Goupia glabra* and its eDNA footprint with Sper01. White
crossed circles are the stems of the botanical survey.

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5}
# Parameters of the five grids, see grid.R
config_tab <- bind_rows(
  list(Metric = "Presence", Radius = 20, Norm = FALSE),
  list(Metric = "Count", Radius = 20, Norm = TRUE),
  list(Metric = "HYP", Radius = 10000, Alpha = 1.79, Norm = TRUE),
  list(Metric = "EXP", Radius = 10000, Alpha = 1.79, Beta = 0.1, Norm = TRUE)
) %>%
  mutate(Type = "bota", Year = "2012") %>%
  bind_rows(list(Type = "genet", Metric = "Reads", Rar = TRUE, Marker = "Sper01", Norm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Level = "Species", Name = "Goupia glabra")

titles <- list(
  expression(bold("1 / 0"~"("~R==20~")")),
  expression(bold(Count~"("~R==20~")")),
  expression(bold(HYP~"("~alpha==1.79~")")),
  expression(bold(EXP~"("~alpha==1.79~","~beta==0.1~")")),
  "Sper01 Reads"
)

plot_list <- Map(function(grid, title){
  plot_grid(grid, stems = TRUE) +
    labs(title = title)
}, build_grids(config_tab), titles)

wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 5)
```

## Figure 7 {#figure-7}

Correlations between the botanical and eDNA patterns, by taxonomic level, marker
and method. Each point is a taxon. 18S is not shown: it only shares 3 taxa with
the botanical survey.

```{r figure-7, fig.height = 7}
df_H3 %>%
  filter(
    Level %in% c("Family","Genus","Species"),
    g.Marker %in% c("Sper01","ITS2"),
    Metric_corr %in% c("I.O","Count","HYP","EXP")
  ) %>%
  corr_violin_plot()
```

## Figure 8 {#figure-8}

Pearson correlation between the morphological traits and the correlation of each
taxon in `df_H3`, for Sper01 with the presence method (I.O) and for ITS2 with the
exponential model (EXP). It shows which traits are linked with a good match
between the eDNA and the stems. Traits are medians by taxon, and their colors
give the organ: leaves in green, stems in orange, roots in brown.

```{r figure-8, fig.height = 9}
p_Sper01 <- morpho_corr_bar_strip(df_H3, Marker = "Sper01", Metric = "I.O", Corr = "pearson") +
  labs(title = "Sper01 / I.O")

p_ITS2 <- morpho_corr_bar_strip(df_H3, Marker = "ITS2", Metric = "EXP", Corr = "pearson") +
  labs(title = "ITS2 / EXP")

p_Sper01 / p_ITS2
```

# Diversity patterns

## Figure 9 {#figure-9}

Spearman correlation between the botanical and eDNA diversity (H1), at each
position, when the botanical diversity is computed within a radius from 5 to
50 m. It shows which radius gives the best match with the soil eDNA.

```{r figure-9}
df_H4 <- cached("df_H4", recompute = RECOMPUTE, function(){

  config_rad <- expand.grid(
    "g.Rar" = TRUE,
    "g.Marker" = c("Sper01","ITS2"),
    "g.Metric" = "H1",
    "b.Radius" = seq(5,50,5),
    "b.Year" = 2012,
    "b.Metric" = "H1",
    "Metric_corr" = "OTU",
    "Level" = c("Species", "Genus", "Family"),
    "Name" = "All",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  make_cor_table(config_rad)
})

plot_correlogramme(df_H4)
```

## Figure 10 {#figure-10}

Diversity patterns of the plot: (a) botanical species richness within a radius
of 5 m, (b) and (c) MOTU diversity (H1) with Sper01 and ITS2. The three maps are
compared with Spearman correlations.

```{r figure-10, fig.height = 5}
# -- Grids --
bota_grid <- grid_read(list(
  Type = "bota",
  Year = "2012",
  Radius = 5,
  Metric = "OTU",
  Level = "Species",
  Name = "All"))

Sper01_grid <- grid_read(list(
  Type = "genet",
  Rar = TRUE,
  Marker = "Sper01",
  Metric = "H1",
  Level = "Species",
  Name = "All"))

ITS2_grid <- grid_read(list(
  Type = "genet",
  Rar = TRUE,
  Marker = "ITS2",
  Metric = "H1",
  Level = "Species",
  Name = "All"))

# -- Maps --
p1 <- plot_grid_interp_soft(bota_grid) +
  labs(title = "(a)", caption = "", fill = "Spe.Rich.")

p2 <- plot_grid_interp_soft(Sper01_grid) +
  labs(title = "(b)", caption = "", fill = "H1")

p3 <- plot_grid_interp_soft(ITS2_grid) +
  labs(title = "(c)", caption = "", fill = "H1")

p1 | p2 | p3

# -- Correlations --
cor.test(bota_grid$df$Metric, Sper01_grid$df$Metric, method = "spearman")
cor.test(bota_grid$df$Metric, ITS2_grid$df$Metric, method = "spearman")
cor.test(Sper01_grid$df$Metric, ITS2_grid$df$Metric, method = "spearman")
```

## Figure 11 {#figure-11}

Relative importance of the edaphic and light conditions on the three diversity
patterns, from 100 random forests of 500 trees. Letters give the Dunn pairwise
tests between patterns for each variable (p < 0.05). The eDNA patterns are those
of Figure 10. The saved forests of the report use the botanical richness within
a radius of 10 m, unlike the 5 m of Figure 10.

```{r figure-11, fig.height = 7}
# Environmental variables at each position
abiotic <- import_abiotic() %>%
  dplyr::select(x,y,wetness,Al,K,Ca,Na,Fe,C,N,light) %>%
  mutate(CNratio = C / N) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(C,N))

df_RF <- cached("df_RF", recompute = RECOMPUTE, function(){

  # Botanical richness within 10 m, the radius of the forests of the report
  bota_grid_RF <- grid_read(list(
    Type = "bota",
    Year = "2012",
    Radius = 10,
    Metric = "OTU",
    Level = "Species",
    Name = "All"))
  
  # Random forests of a diversity pattern
  run_forests <- function(grid, pattern){
    inner_join(grid$df, abiotic, by = c("x","y")) %>%
      rand_for_IncMSE_rep() %>%
      mutate(pattern = pattern)
  }

  bind_rows(
    run_forests(bota_grid_RF, "Bota"),
    run_forests(Sper01_grid, "Sper01"),
    run_forests(ITS2_grid, "ITS2")
  )
})

plot_RF_stat(df_RF)
```

Taxa shared between the reference checklist, the botanical survey and the

## Figure S2 {#figure-s2}

Relative richness by family in each survey. Only proportions above 0.5% are
displayed, and those above 2% are in bold.

```{r figure-s2, fig.height = 11}
family_richness_list(df_H1, ref_label = "Ref") %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(Metric = round(Metric, digits = 2)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!Metric < 0.5) %>%
  ab_rel_tab()
```

## Figure S3 {#figure-s3}

Distribution of the morphological traits. The stars give the significance of the
Shapiro normality test: * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001.

```{r figure-s3, fig.height = 8}
plot_trait_distribution(import_plants_morpho())
```

## Figure S4 {#figure-s4}

Correlation matrix of the morphological traits. Only correlations above 0.5 and
below -0.5 are displayed.

```{r figure-s4, fig.height = 8}
import_plants_morpho() %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") %>%
  plot_corr_triangle(threshold = 0.5, y_labels = trait_labels())
```

## Figure S5 {#figure-s5}

Correlation matrix of the environmental drivers used in the random forests.

```{r figure-s5}
abiotic %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(x,y)) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs") %>%
  plot_corr_triangle(threshold = 0.1, fill_label = "Pearson r")
```
